record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.context_brief: Nature of S11(1535) and eta-nucleon scattering
record.original_question: What is the physical nature of the S11(1535) resonance that dominates eta-meson production from single nucleons: is it a compact quark-model baryon state, a dynamically generated state, or specifically an eta-nucleon molecular state? A self-contained resolution should explain how the energy dependence of the elastic eta-nucleon scattering amplitude in the eta-nucleon channel can distinguish a molecule from a compact state, despite the fact that direct elastic eta-nucleon scattering is experimentally inaccessible, and should derive useful constraints on the eta-nucleon scattering parameters from available non-diagonal hadronic and photon-induced reactions.

evidence.quote: It is well known that the production of eta mesons from single nucleons is dominated by the resonance S11(1535) irrespective of the probe.

Especially since the nature of this resonance is heavily debated in the literature (see also next section and references given there), a systematic study of η production in various environments is of high importance.

How is it possible to distinguish molecular states and compact quark states? Based on an old proposal by Weinberg [17] in Ref. [18], in line with a series of older works [19], we identified the energy dependence of the elastic scattering amplitude in the molecule forming channel as a key quantity.
Thus, to understand if the S11 is an ηN molecule, experimental information is needed on elastic ηN scattering. Unfortunately this channel is not directly accessible.

To summarize the investigations based on reactions on a single baryon we state that in order to better understand the nature of the S11(1535) both high accuracy data and theoretical studies are necessary to derive constraints on the ηN scattering parameters.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nucleon resonance commonly labeled S11(1535): a spin-1/2, negative-parity, isospin-1/2 baryon resonance with mass near 1535 MeV that couples strongly to the ηN channel and dominates η-meson production off single nucleons by hadronic and electromagnetic probes near threshold.

Two competing structural hypotheses are to be distinguished:
(i) a compact three-quark state, as in standard constituent quark models;
(ii) a dynamically generated meson–baryon (in particular ηN, KΛ, KΣ) quasi-bound state — a "molecular" state — produced by coupled-channel hadronic interactions.

Following Weinberg's compositeness criterion, the residue and energy dependence of the elastic scattering amplitude T_{ηN→ηN}(E) near the resonance pole encode the probability that the physical state is dominated by the ηN two-hadron component: a purely molecular ηN state implies specific low-energy parameters (scattering length a_{ηN}, effective range r_{ηN}, and a characteristic shape of T_{ηN→ηN}) that differ sharply from those of a compact state weakly coupled to the ηN continuum.

The problem is the following.

(A) Determine, in a model-independent way using Weinberg's compositeness argument, the precise quantitative criterion on the elastic ηN amplitude (and equivalently on the pair (a_{ηN}, r_{ηN})) that distinguishes an ηN molecular interpretation of S11(1535) from a compact three-quark interpretation.

(B) Since direct elastic ηN scattering is not experimentally accessible (no η beams or targets), derive constraints on the elastic ηN amplitude — in particular on a_{ηN} and r_{ηN} — from available non-diagonal hadronic and photon-induced reactions producing ηN final states (e.g. πN → ηN, γN → ηN, NN → NNη, γd → ηX, η-production on nuclei), using analyticity, unitarity, and final-state interaction arguments.

(C) Apply these constraints to decide whether the S11(1535) is best described as a compact quark-model baryon, a dynamically generated state, or specifically an ηN molecular state.
artifact.status_search_result: The nature of N*(1535)/S11(1535) remains actively debated. A 2024 study (Eur. Phys. J. C) explicitly contrasts observables for the molecular versus genuine three-quark interpretations and proposes measurements of scattering length and effective range to discriminate between them, indicating that the question has not been definitively resolved. Coupled-channel and lattice studies have produced supporting evidence on both sides, but no consensus exists.

status_evidence.title: Contrasting observables related to the N*(1535) from the molecular or a genuine structure
status_evidence.snippet: Predictions of the two pictures are drastically different; measurements of scattering lengths and effective ranges are advised to gain valuable information concerning the nature of this state.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work treats the molecular-vs-compact nature of N*(1535) as still unresolved and proposes discriminating observables.

status_evidence.title: Roper Resonance and S11(1535) from lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice QCD investigation of the S11(1535) structure.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing lattice and model studies continue to probe the structure of S11(1535), indicating unresolved status.
